habit_scope: alternate in all regions. Model-code and HUD accepted (AF&PA Wood Foundations; ORNL Ch 2 notes 26–30; HUD Fig 4.9 / Table 4.8). Not the regional default.
how_it_is_done: Site / termite prep still applies: organics out; soil treatment where hazard; do not trade treatment for shields (D8).
Gravel bed ≥4 in (AF&PA Wood Foundations) / ≥6 in thick and 6 in past the plate (ORNL note 27). Compacted.
Treated footing plate on the stone.

Treated studs + plywood; joints caulked; 6-mil on basement walls (AF&PA; ORNL notes 26–30). This is a treated system per the wood-foundation standard — not a field-cut untreated wall (HUD §4.5 / Fig 4.9).

Gravel under the floor to a center sump (24 in deep, 16 in dia or square) to daylight or pump. D9 agreement: no conventional drain tile around a footing — gravel to sump (AF&PA Wood Foundations; ORNL notes 26–30 citing NFPA 1987). Coarse gravel against the lower half of the wall (ORNL).
Slab or treated wood floor over 6-mil (AF&PA; ORNL notes 28–30, 36). PWF may use a treated wood floor in lieu of a basement slab.
Batt in cavities; 2-in air gap above the bottom plate (ORNL note 35).
Winter / prefab is the reason to pick it (AF&PA Wood Foundations).

HUD: treated lumber/plywood per the wood-foundation standard
tools_equipment: Not a tool list in sources.
inspection_hold_points: Treated material and gravel-bed thickness before walls (AF&PA; ORNL note 27).
No drain tile to look for — inspect gravel path to sump instead (D9).
6-mil on basement walls and under floor.
PWF / treated-wall system on drawings before permit (HUD Fig 4.9 / Table 4.8).
material_classes_notes: Drain tile is NOT used with PWF (D9). Do not shop drain tile for this method.
when_this_beats_habit: Winter or prefab schedule (AF&PA). Cold-weather pours are the thing it avoids. Accepted by model codes and HUD as a full system, not a one-off.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Not the regional default in Wasatch (basement) or Fontana (slab). Do not add conventional footing drain tile — that is a D9 miss. Do not field-cut untreated walls and call it PWF.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: Yards and crews in these three markets are CIP/CMU or SOG. PWF is a treated-system specialty; winter/prefab is the usual reason anyone switches.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
risk_if_swapped_late: PWF vs CIP/CMU after permit changes excavation, drainage (no tile), treated package, and inspection path. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: This is the treated-wood basement or crawl: gravel bed, treated plate and studs, plywood, plastic, gravel to a sump. No drain tile. People pick it to prefab or to keep pouring out of a winter hole. It is legal; it is not what Wasatch or Fontana usually builds.
spanish_summary: Cimiento de madera tratada: cama de grava, placa y postes tratados, plywood, plástico, grava hasta un sumidero. No lleva tubo de drenaje. Se usa para prefabricar o para no colar en invierno. Es legal, no es lo habitual aquí.
d9_agreement: No conventional footing tile; gravel + sump. Filed as agreement, not a disagreement winner.
confidence_notes: D9 no-tile + gravel/sump agreed AF&PA and ORNL (high). Sequence sourced. Not volume habit.

fastener_schedule_notes: Re-checked AF&PA Wood Foundations (Figs 6–7) and HUD Fig 4.9 / Table 4.8. HUD Fig 4.9 prints “NAIL AND/OR FRAMING ANCHORS AS REQUIRED” with no size+oc. Table 4.8 is stud size/spacing (2x6 @ 16 in / 5 ft backfill; 2x6 @ 12 in / 6 ft; 2x8 @ 12 in / 8 ft) plus “connect each stud to top plate with framing anchors when backfill height is 6 feet or greater” — no penny, no oc. HUD: all PWF fasteners/hardware stainless steel or hot-dipped galvanized (coating, not a schedule). AF&PA Figs 6–7 silent on penny/oc; points to AF&PA TR-7 / Southern Pine PWF guide / AF&PA 2007 spec. Do not invent 8d/10d/16d. fastener_schedule stays []. gap-sop-fastener-missing keeps m-P05-pwf.
